title: Complexe de De Rham à puissance divisée [conférence de 1976 à l’IHÉS] : notes manuscrites (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
This page continues the comparison of four complexes built from a module M over a commutative ring A:
(1) the de Rham complex Sym*M ⊗ Λ*M;
(2) the Koszul complex on Sym*M;
(3) the divided-power de Rham complex Γ*M ⊗ Λ*M;
(4) the Koszul complex on Γ*M.

First, a general Koszul construction. Let S be a commutative ring, 𝓜 an S-module and φ: 𝓜 → S an S-linear form. Then there is a unique antiderivation δ of the exterior algebra Λ*_S 𝓜 that restricts to φ on Λ^1, and δ² = 0. This is the Koszul complex K(φ).
- H_0 = S/φ(𝓜).
- For 𝓜 free of finite type, H_i = 0 for i ≠ 0 exactly when φ is 'transversal'. It suffices that the images of a basis form an S-regular sequence. This is also necessary if S is noetherian and φ(𝓜) ⊂ rad S.

Complexes (2) and (4) are the cases S = Sym*M (resp. Γ*M), 𝓜 = M ⊗_A S, with φ given by multiplication through M ≅ S^1 ⊂ S. Concretely, δ(s ⊗ x1∧…∧xq) = Σ ± s·xi ⊗ x1∧…x̂i…∧xq.

Next Grothendieck forms θ = dδ + δd on S* ⊗ Λ*.
- d has bidegree (−1,+1) and δ has bidegree (+1,−1). Both are odd antiderivations, so their anticommutator θ is an even derivation preserving bidegree.
- θ is the identity on generators. For x ∈ S^1: dx = 1⊗x and δ(1⊗x) = x. For ξ ∈ Λ^1: δξ ∈ S^1 and d(δξ) = ξ.
- When S = Γ, θ is a PD-derivation, so θ(x^[k]) = x^[k−1]·x = k·x^[k].
- Hence θ is the Euler operator: θ = n·Id on the total-degree-n part ⊕_{p+q=n} S^p ⊗ Λ^q.

Since θ is null-homotopic for both d and δ, each total-degree-n summand of the de Rham and Koszul complexes is contractible whenever n·1_A is invertible. In particular, in characteristic 0, H^n_DR and H_n^Kosz vanish for n > 0, with no flatness hypothesis on M; there Sym ≅ Γ.

The purpose is to compute the cohomology of the four complexes and their relations; the de Rham complex of divided powers is the topic of the 1976 IHÉS talk. The next page settles H^0 via the same homotopy and introduces the duality Sym*M ↔ Γ*M', under which d and δ are transposes.
errors: No substantive mathematical errors. The transversality criterion is stated loosely, with 'transversal' undefined; it is the standard Koszul-regularity criterion.
The phrase 'en changeant le bidegré' should read 'ne changeant pas le bidegré': θ preserves bidegree, as the subsequent Euler formula requires.

ideas.what: Koszul complex of a linear form φ: 𝓜 → S as the unique square-zero antiderivation of Λ𝓜 extending φ; acyclicity iff regular sequence (necessity in the noetherian/radical case)
ideas.modern_name: Koszul complex K(φ); depth-sensitivity / regular-sequence criterion
ideas.usually_credited_to: Koszul; Serre (Algèbre locale, multiplicités), Bourbaki Alg. X
ideas.where_published: EGA IV (0_IV §15 / 16.x on Koszul complexes and regular sequences), SGA 6 Exp. VII

ideas.what: Realizing the Koszul resolutions Sym⊗Λ and Γ⊗Λ as Koszul complexes of the tautological form M⊗S → S
ideas.modern_name: Koszul complexes of Sym and Γ (Koszul duality Sym/Λ, Γ/Λ)
ideas.usually_credited_to: Illusie (Complexe cotangent I, Ch. I §4.3), Cartan seminar

ideas.what: θ = dδ + δd is a (PD-)derivation equal to the identity on generators, hence the Euler operator n·Id in total degree n; contractibility wherever n is invertible, without flatness
ideas.modern_name: Euler/Cartier homotopy formula (Poincaré lemma in char 0 for de Rham and Koszul complexes)
ideas.usually_credited_to: classical (Cartier homotopy); Illusie, Complexe cotangent I; Berthelot for the PD Poincaré lemma

deep.surprise_reason: Clean but standard material: the Koszul complex of a linear form and the Euler-operator homotopy dδ + δd = n giving acyclicity where n is invertible. All of it is classical (Koszul, Cartier, Illusie, Berthelot) and is preparatory to the PD de Rham talk.
transcription_corrections: Λ̌ / $\check{\Lambda}$ throughout is Grothendieck's $\overset{*}{\Lambda}$ (exterior algebra with a star), matching the previous page's notation.
'en changeant [-pas le-] le bidegré' should be read as 'ne changeant pas le bidegré' (θ preserves bidegree).
'(étant anticommutant de antidérivations chacune une dérivation)' is better read as an anticommutator of two antidérivations ('anticommutateur de deux antidérivations'), hence a derivation.
'H_0(...) = S/φ(M)' uses script 𝓢 and 𝓜 for the ring and module of the general Koszul set-up.
